purpose: Durable per-workspace shared-safety capacity authority. One complete workspace_capacity row carries the current defaults revision/digest, monotonic authority revision and regional capacity fence; immutable capacity_audit rows retain every committed decision identity. The controller atomically writes this authority together with the complete public effective-limit projection.

serverSideEncryption.rationale: Capacity decisions are a regional authority with a distinct write role and recovery boundary; they must not share the session or authorization-projection key authority.

globalSecondaryIndexes.name: gsi_all_workspaces
globalSecondaryIndexes.rationale: The enumeration a defaults-revision sweep walks. Only the `workspace_capacity` authority row carries `gsiAllPk`, so an immutable `capacity_audit` sibling can never appear in a sweep and be reconciled twice. Both attributes were already written on every commit and indexed by nothing, which left the ordered `Reconcile` sweep undeliverable: a limit id added after a workspace was bootstrapped reaches it only through that sweep, and nothing could enumerate the workspaces to run it over. The projection is KEYS_ONLY because a sweep needs an identity and then reads the authority row it is about to condition on strongly anyway.

stream.rationale: Capacity commands are explicit direct invokes and publish their serving projection in the same transaction; there is no asynchronous second writer to catch up.

timeToLive.rationale: An expired authority or audit row would either fail every request or erase the evidence for an override, so neither family is TTL data.

condition.rationale: The leading-key fence is the table's. The sweep index has one partition, `WORKSPACES`, and is KEYS_ONLY, so a query over it can enumerate workspace identities and nothing else; fencing it on `WS#*` would deny the enumeration outright while protecting a keyspace the index does not expose.
